To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sex composition of children desired in the future is influenced by both cultural and individual factors.

son preference is declining in both Australia and Malaysia, and that this is due to a decline in the importance of traditional reasons for wanting a boy, and an increase in the importance of psychological reasons for wanting a girl.

(i) the sex preference for children is higher for parents in Malaysia than Australia; (ii) the sex preference of Malaysian parents is for sons; (iii) the sex preference in Australia varies according to ethnicity, being highest for Greek parents and lowest for Australian-born parents; (iv) the main reason for preferring a son is for the support that a son will provide in old age; (v) the main reason that parents prefer a daughter is for her companionship.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the value of children, the motivations for wanting children and the sex preferences of parents.
the role of values and disvalues in explaining fertility decline.
the role of the family and the value of the child in the transition to low fertility.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no simple relationship between the fertility of a country and the value of children.
there has been a change from the traditional role of children to a more psychological one, but that this change is not uniform and varies across countries and ethnic groups.
son preference is declining in Australia and Malaysia and that this is occurring in the context of a shift from traditional to psychological values in the benefits of children.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in both countries there is evidence of a shift in the value of children from traditional to modern values, but that the transition in values is not complete.

the value of children has changed from a focus on traditional roles to more psychological benefits of children in high fertility societies to a greater concern with the traditional benefits of children in low fertility societies.
the transition to low fertility has not yet been accompanied by a transition to a new set of values and disvalues.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there is a need to examine the motivations for wanting children in the context of the social, cultural and historical background of the parents.
